reason: I downloaded the djvu text of archive.org item the-myth-of-sisyphus_202509 myself (title page: Justin O’Brien, 1st Vintage International ed.). On p. 202, Return to Tipasa, the sentence reads: In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer. That matches the card to the letter. The printed ornament comes straight after it and the next paragraph opens I have again left Tipasa. That ornament is the only section break in the essay (pp. 193 to 203), so the end of the first section is right. The attribution is right: Camus speaks in his own voice, and the popular in the depths of winter wording is Ellen Conroy Kennedy’s (Lyrical and Critical Essays, 1968), not O’Brien’s. Nothing on the misattribution list touches it. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Camus at 1 of 3 (month 1), not banned. The source line is 129 characters, leads with the name, has no dash and names the translator; the tag Essay is the form. It is famous and fits hope. Two soft points, neither a refutation. First, a note naming the Kennedy rival wording would stop a reader filing it as a misquotation. Second, the editor must choose between this and the Camus carry-in 02-cfl-07 only if the no-person-twice-in-a-month rule bites; the yearly cap does not.
